clue.text: 1D/30 covered my flight and one limo stateside

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a limousine is a kind of car
stateside means in the United States, abbreviated US

explanation.surface: A band boasts of having sung about the narrator's own flight, then a limo ride in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 1D/30 is Iron Maiden, whose song Flight of Icarus tells the myth; 'my flight' is the flight as Icarus himself would name it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Maiden's song Flight of Icarus is about the mythical youth whose wax wings melted, so its subject is that flier.

clue.text: Press gets mean over rockers from Leyton

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them
in cricket a maiden over concedes no runs, so it is a mean, stingy over

explanation.surface: The press turns nasty about some rock musicians from a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, but it describes a cricket over: a maiden is an over of six balls from which the batters score nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Maiden, the heavy metal band, was formed in Leyton in East London in 1975.

clue.text: Cards or flyers

blocks.note: first meaning: the top cards of each suit in a pack
second meaning: expert fighter pilots with many kills

explanation.walkthrough: A nod to the theme too: Aces High is an Iron Maiden song about fighter pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the single-pip playing cards and star wartime pilots credited with downing several enemy planes.

clue.text: Peacekeepers gauge units oddly delivered ointment

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in the odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: United Nations troops act as peacekeepers
the odd letters across both words

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops, measuring their supplies erratically, handed out some cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters run across both words, ignoring the space between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Unguent is a formal or medical word for a soothing salve or ointment rubbed on the skin.

clue.text: Like much ground hamburger, principally kosher

indicators.note: principally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is used

blocks.note: its opening letter
kosher can mean permitted or legitimate

explanation.surface: Minced beef, like a burger, mostly prepared to Jewish dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like minced meat beside hamburger, but it is the noun in the phrase hallowed ground. Hallowed Be Thy Name is an Iron Maiden song.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed ground is the stock phrase for consecrated land, so much ground is described with this adjective.

clue.text: A culture paper covering independent cartoons

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the New Musical Express, a music and culture weekly
I is the standard abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: An arts magazine reviewing independent animated films.
explanation.walkthrough: The NME (New Musical Express) is a British music paper; it wraps around I, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is the Japanese style of animation, so its films and series are cartoons.

clue.text: Light bag stashed in string instrument

indicators.note: something stashed in another thing is tucked away inside it

blocks.note: a lute is a plucked string instrument
to net is to catch or bag

explanation.surface: A lightweight case hidden inside a guitar or violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as an adjective for the bag, but it is the noun, a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a crescent or half-moon shaped window, an architectural light set into a vault or above a door.

clue.text: Hair removable with Instagram

blocks.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
IG is the common shorthand for Instagram

explanation.surface: Unwanted hair can be got rid of with a social media filter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig is a head of false hair that can be taken off, unlike one's own.

clue.text: Cleaners put off by little boy's room

blocks.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a jokey phrase for the men's toilet, the gents in Britain

explanation.surface: Cleaning staff are repelled by the state of the men's lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaners' looks like people, but the answer is the substances that do the cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergents are washing agents, the products that clean clothes and dishes.

clue.text: Bunch of old-fashioned geezers apt to lose it

indicators.note: a bunch of things is a gathering of some of them, so a run of letters is taken from the words after

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A group of fogeyish old men who are liable to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Geezer is British slang for a man, often an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on edge is tense and nervous, close to losing their composure.

clue.text: Where good may be found in the darkest hour?

definitions.text: Where good may be found in the darkest hour?

blocks.note: surface reading: hope or virtue shining through at a bleak moment
setter's reading: good is G, which sits in the centre of the word night, and the darkest hour is twelve at night

explanation.walkthrough: G is the usual abbreviation for good. The clue also nods to Iron Maiden's 2 Minutes to Midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the night, twelve o'clock, is traditionally thought of as the darkest hour.

clue.text: Skyscraper could be feet lower if reworked

indicators.note: reworked means remade in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An architect muses that a tall building could be made shorter if the plans were revised.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris landmark is a very tall structure, loosely a skyscraper, and was the world's tallest building when finished.

clue.text: Pyrotechnic style on record

indicators.note: something on record has been spoken and captured as sound, so the word is judged by how it is said

blocks.note: flair is a stylish talent or panache

explanation.surface: A dazzling, fiery performance style captured on an album.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare is a firework-like signal light, a piece of pyrotechnics, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Talk's provider seemed primarily useless

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the word just before is put at the front

blocks.note: to be or appear: seemed loosely means was
TED is the organisation behind TED Talks

explanation.surface: The person laying on the talk came across as mainly hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' looks like it wants a first letter, but it moves the word before it to the front. Wasted Years is an Iron Maiden song.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort that is wasted is to no purpose, so it is useless or squandered.

clue.text: Beat Albion on the pitch? It's within reach!

indicators.note: a team on the pitch is in play and moving about, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan believes victory over Albion in the match is there for the taking.
explanation.walkthrough: Albion is the nickname of several English football clubs, such as West Bromwich Albion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obtainable can be got, so it is attainable or within reach.

clue.text: Loud McBrain sheds layer playing material

indicators.note: shedding a layer means losing the outside covering, so the first and last letters go
playing suggests the letters are tossed about and arranged afresh

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
Nicko McBrain is Iron Maiden's drummer

explanation.surface: A thunderous drummer strips off a layer of clothing while performing.
explanation.walkthrough: Without its outer M and N, McBrain leaves CBRAI, which is rearranged after F.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, the woven or knitted material clothes are made from.

clue.text: Monster hit featuring Smith's lead

indicators.note: featuring means including, so one piece is held within the other
the lead of something is its front, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: to beat is to hit
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A huge chart success with Smith on lead guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a guitar part (Adrian Smith plays guitar in Iron Maiden) but takes a first letter. The Number of the Beast is a Maiden album.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is a savage creature, a synonym for a monster.

clue.text: Person contacted to clothe Eddie's outside behind trailer

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two ends, so its first and last letters are kept
behind means following on, so what comes next is placed after the first piece

blocks.note: a trailer is an advertisement for a film, an ad
to clothe someone is to dress them
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is phoned to dress Eddie for the outdoors, round the back of a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a caravan but is a film preview. Eddie is Iron Maiden's zombie mascot.
explanation.definitionFit: An addressee is the person a letter or message is directed to, the one being contacted.

clue.text: Protest over bass split up the band

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march or demonstration
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A row about the bass player broke the group up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' means placed on top of the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob is to demobilise, releasing troops from service, so a military band of soldiers is disbanded.

clue.text: Current AI adds smarter processing

indicators.note: processing works material over into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
adds means puts alongside, so one piece is joined to the next

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Up-to-date artificial intelligence brings more sophisticated data handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning up to date, but it is a noun: a flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstream is a flow or current of air, such as the wind behind a moving vehicle.

clue.text: 1D/30 character reflected on unfortunate time

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: re means on, concerning
a poor soul is an unfortunate one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone from the band thought back on a bad period.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trooper is an Iron Maiden song about a cavalryman in the Charge of the Light Brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: The cavalry soldier is the figure the Maiden song The Trooper is sung by and about.

clue.text: Unresponsive Milan side tense into the finish

indicators.note: into the finish means sent to the end, so that letter moves to the final place

blocks.note: Inter Milan is a football club in Milan
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An Italian football team seems lifeless, nervous as the end of the match approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The T already inside the club's name moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert is without movement or reaction, so it does not respond.

clue.text: Iconic beach beer I agree to raise

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters upward, so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: IPA is India pale ale, a beer
amen means so be it, I agree

explanation.surface: Someone at a famous beach agrees to lift a glass of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like a separate letter but belongs to the phrase whose meaning is amen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipanema in Rio de Janeiro is a world-famous beach, celebrated in the song The Girl from Ipanema.

clue.text: Fear Of The Dark band's first hit on a copy for broadcast

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word before is taken
broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: its opening letter
taken as written, ready to rearrange

explanation.surface: Iron Maiden's song Fear of the Dark, a big hit, is covered for radio play.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make the definition look like a song title, which it also is: Fear of the Dark is a Maiden hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyctophobia is the medical term, from Greek nyx (night), for an abnormal dread of darkness or night.

clue.text: Harris gutted about bad parts in 1D/30 song

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the first and last letters
about means around, so the outer letters go either side of the next piece

blocks.note: its first and last letters
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Steve Harris, the band's bassist, is upset about the poor bits of one of their songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Iron Maiden's song Run to the Hills supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hills are the places named in the title of the Maiden song Run to the Hills.

clue.text: Flashy playing won Murray admirers in seconds

indicators.note: in seconds points to the second letter of each word in turn

blocks.note: its second letter
its second letter
its second letter
its second letter

explanation.surface: Showy play quickly won over fans of Murray.
explanation.walkthrough: Murray suggests the tennis player Andy, but Dave Murray is Iron Maiden's guitarist; 'seconds' means second letters, not a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud describes clothes or colours that are garish and showy, just as flashy does.

clue.text: Intense piercing

blocks.note: first meaning: eager and strongly felt
second meaning: sharp

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a stare, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both strong enthusiasm or feeling and sharpness of an edge, wind or sense.

clue.text: Place crushed by King Kong?

indicators.note: something crushed by another is squeezed inside its grip, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: King Kong is the giant gorilla of the 1933 film, a huge ape
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A movie fan wonders which spot the giant ape flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: King Kong rampages through New York and climbs the Empire State Building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is New York City's nickname, the city the film's giant gorilla wrecks.

clue.text: Gers quitting halfway through long set

indicators.note: quitting halfway through means stopping at the midpoint, so only the first half of the word survives

blocks.note: Janick Gers is one of Iron Maiden's guitarists
L is an abbreviation for longitude, written long.

explanation.surface: A guitarist walks off midway through a lengthy concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long set' reads as a concert, but set is the definition, a verb meaning to solidify.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly or a mixture that sets becomes firm, and to gel is to do exactly that.

clue.text: Crack work from Dickinson after cold month

indicators.note: after means following, so the piece before this word is placed second

blocks.note: December, a winter month, abbreviated
an ode is a poem, the sort of work the poet Emily Dickinson wrote

explanation.surface: Solving a piece by Dickinson, after a chilly month.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickinson also nods to Bruce Dickinson, Iron Maiden's singer.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code or cipher is to decode it, working out its hidden message.

clue.text: Joy about metal starting late growth offshore

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word before is read backwards
starting late means missing the beginning, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: glee is joy or delight
brass is an alloy of copper and zinc

explanation.surface: Delight at heavy metal music arriving late in a career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metal' suggests the music the puzzle celebrates, but here it is a real metal alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eelgrass is a marine flowering plant that grows in shallow coastal waters, a growth found just offshore.
